question: Should Workspaces permanently expose `bus:pubsub` as one capability granting approved widgets both publish and subscribe access to arbitrary channels within their current tab?
rationale: The code can enforce the proposed boundary, but choosing the durable widget API and deciding whether a whole tab is one trusted messaging domain require maintainer product and security intent.

options.title: Sponsor current contract
options.body: Accept the tab as the messaging trust domain, document that all `bus:pubsub` widgets may exchange arbitrary channel payloads, and require feature-specific browser proof before merge.

options.title: Narrow the contract
options.body: Split publish and subscribe permissions or declare allowed channels in the manifest before exposing the API to widget authors.

options.title: Defer pub/sub
options.body: Keep custom widgets isolated and close or pause this PR until a stronger cross-widget capability model is prioritized.

recommendation.title: Sponsor current contract
recommendation.body: Accept the tab as the messaging trust domain, document that all `bus:pubsub` widgets may exchange arbitrary channel payloads, and require feature-specific browser proof before merge.

likelyOwner.reason: The merged Workspaces foundation and its custom-widget security boundary are most directly associated with this recent feature integration.
